blockerTitle: Independent verifier missing omitted qualifying condition
productionFreezeShaNote: 22-recertification-baseline.json names d098cb4 as the freeze SHA; this worktree's HEAD is 2663271, which the task brief states (and this audit did not modify any production file, so this is not independently re-verified byte-for-byte here) is byte-identical to d098cb4 in every production file, adding only one documentation artifact on top.
mandate: Independently construct 10-15 NEW condition-language forms not covered by Part A Workstream E's own 43-test suite; directly attack the isSynthetic gate; re-verify verifier independence by tracing data flow rather than trusting the prior report; re-run the original 7-case fault-injection reproduction against current code.

task1_novelConditionForms.methodology: 12 condition-phrasing forms constructed, all deliberately disjoint from (a) the original 9-form matrix (tests/contract-model/semantic-verification-condition-remediation.test.ts) and (b) Part A Workstream E's own 12-form / 43-test matrix (tests/contract-model/semantic-verification-condition-remediation-rx.test.ts). Each form was first probed directly against the real buildSourceInventory function (not assumed), then, for forms not detected at Layer 1a, run through the REAL, unmodified verifyCompiledCandidate with no options overrides (exact production call shape) on a rule that drops its own real condition entirely while its dollar figure still reconciles, to determine whether a DIFFERENT mechanism (numeric reconciliation, structural-completeness signal) nonetheless catches the drop, or whether the candidate reaches an uncontested false clean pass.

formsCaught.form: nested multi-clause proviso: "provided that, notwithstanding the foregoing, if and only if..."
formsCaught.result: CAUGHT - matches three already-covered constituent markers ("provided that", "notwithstanding", "if and only if") simultaneously; confirms nested/compound provisos do not confuse or double-count the detector.
CAUGHT - matched via the substring "unless" (word-boundary safe).

formsCaught.form: "if, but only if" (a comma-interrupted variant of "if and only if" neither prior matrix tested)
formsCaught.result: CAUGHT - matched via the substring "only if".

formsNotCaughtBySourceInventoryLayer: upon the occurrence of [a defined trigger] (e.g. a Change of Control) - extremely common credit-agreement condition idiom; distinct from the "(?:following|upon)\s+satisfaction\s+of" pattern RX Part A added, which requires the word "satisfaction"
"as and when" paired with "following" - "following" alone (without a trailing "satisfaction of") is not in the pattern list
passive voice: "shall be deemed satisfied when" - bare "when" is not a detected marker
a condition expressed purely as a capitalized DEFINED TERM trigger ("Upon the Trigger Event,") with no other connective word from the pattern list at all
a condition incorporated purely by schedule cross-reference ("in accordance with the requirements set forth on Schedule 6.01(b)"), with no conditional connective word anywhere in the sentence
"in the event of [a binary trigger]" with no embedded ratio/amount figure inside the condition clause itself
"in the event that [a binary trigger]" with no embedded ratio/amount figure inside the condition clause itself
"to the extent that [a binary trigger]" with no embedded ratio/amount figure inside the condition clause itself
task1_novelConditionForms.endToEndConsequence: For all 8 forms above, constructing a rule that drops its own real condition entirely (conditions: []) while its own dollar capacity figure still reconciles cleanly, and running the REAL, unmodified verifyCompiledCandidate (no test overrides - the exact production call shape), reaches status=VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND with semanticReviewInvoked=false, reconciliation.materialUnresolvedCount=0, and zero findings - a genuine, reproducible false clean pass with the real qualifying condition silently and completely dropped, receiving ZERO scrutiny from either verification layer. This is the exact original BLOCKER-9 failure mode (docs/phase-3f1-6-final-foundation-certification/15-independent-verifier-certification.json's F17-1 'omitted condition' case), reproduced with 8 different, common surface forms neither the original fix (3F.1.6.R) nor Part A Workstream E's own re-attack (3F.1.6.RX) tested or closed.
task1_novelConditionForms.importantNuance_incidentalCapture: "in the event that"/"to the extent that" are NOT closed even when they happen to co-occur with a ratio/amount figure inside the same condition clause (e.g. "to the extent that the Total Leverage Ratio does not exceed 4.00 to 1.00") - that specific variant IS caught end-to-end, but ONLY via reconcileNumericItems flagging the embedded 4.00 RATIO value as NOT_ACCOUNTED_FOR, never via CONDITIONAL_PHRASE recall (independently confirmed: buildSourceInventory raises zero CONDITIONAL_PHRASE/EXCEPTION_MARKER/PROVISO_MARKER items for this exact sentence). This is a coincidental save specific to fact patterns that happen to embed a reconcilable number in the condition text, not a substantive fix of the recall gap - a binary, non-numeric condition using either phrase (as demonstrated in the two dedicated binary-trigger cases above) is not caught by any mechanism.
task1_novelConditionForms.verifiedBy: tests/contract-model/part-b-recert-blocker9-independent-attack.test.ts - 'GENUINE RECALL GAPS' describe block (16 tests: 8 forms x [Layer-1a-no-signal check, end-to-end false-clean-pass check]) plus a dedicated 'coincidental capture' describe block (1 test) and a 'positive controls' describe block (3 tests) for the caught forms.
task1_novelConditionForms.classificationOfFinding: Within BLOCKER-9's own disclosed charter and root-cause class (source-inventory.ts's CONDITIONAL_PHRASE vocabulary list is, and structurally must be, an open-ended, never-provably-exhaustive enumeration of English condition-drafting idiom - this is the same root cause Part A Workstream E itself found and partially patched twice within a single day of work: "until such time as"/"no Event of Default" in 3F.1.6.R, then "conditioned upon"/"following satisfaction of"/"immediately before and after" in 3F.1.6.RX Part A). This is not a new, architecturally distinct defect - it is the SAME defect class recurring with different vocabulary, which is exactly what an independent adversarial recertification pass is supposed to surface. Given 8 distinct, materially common real-world forms (not exotic drafting) still reach an uncontested false clean pass under real default production routing, Part A's own claim that its fix 'generalizes correctly to every new material form tested' does not extend to the broader universe of common condition phrasing, and the underlying architectural weakness (a single, finite, hand-maintained regex list as the ONLY gate that determines whether Layer 2 ever looks at a candidate at all, for a single-rule/non-alternating/numerically-clean candidate) remains genuinely unresolved.

task2_isSyntheticAdversarialAttack.methodology: Constructed a scripted StageCaller that explicitly reports isSynthetic:true while returning an empty findings array with forceSemanticReview:true - deliberately impersonating exactly what the real no-credential SyntheticStageCaller fallback always returns (llm-caller.ts's SyntheticStageCaller.call resolves schema.parse({}) unconditionally). Ran this against a benign single-stray-marker candidate that Part A's own precision fix WOULD legitimately downgrade if the review were genuine.
task2_isSyntheticAdversarialAttack.result: PASS - downgradeUnconfirmedAmbiguousFindings genuinely refuses to downgrade. status stayed REVIEW_REQUIRED (never VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND/VERIFIED_WITH_NON_MATERIAL_FINDINGS), the MISSING_CONDITION finding kept its original UNCERTAIN severity, and its verifierReasoning did not gain the '[downgraded to NON_MATERIAL...]' suffix - confirmed against the ACTUAL code path (verify.ts line: `if (review.failed || review.isSynthetic) return findings;` is the very first line of the function body, an unconditional early return with no other logic preceding it that could be bypassed).
task2_isSyntheticAdversarialAttack.contrastControl: The identical scenario (same text, same empty findings array) but isSynthetic:false DOES legitimately downgrade to NON_MATERIAL - proving the gate keys specifically on the isSynthetic flag, not on some other property of an empty-findings response, and ruling out the possibility that the gate is a no-op that happens to look correct only because a stub's response shape differs from a real one's.
task2_isSyntheticAdversarialAttack.isSyntheticComputationRiskAssessment: Traced to its source: reviewer.ts's runAdversarialSemanticReview returns `isSynthetic: caller.isSynthetic` on BOTH its success and failure return paths (no path drops or defaults this field). llm-caller.ts defines isSynthetic as a hardcoded class-instance field, never a runtime-computed boolean expression: RealStageCaller sets `isSynthetic = false` as a class field initializer (line 32), SyntheticStageCaller sets `isSynthetic = true` as a class field initializer (line 55) - there is no shared code path, no default parameter, and no fallback expression that could silently compute the wrong value for either class. getStageCaller()'s own selection order (AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY -> ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> throw on Vercel -> SyntheticStageCaller) can only ever construct one of these two classes, each with its own fixed, non-configurable isSynthetic literal. This is a structurally low-risk design for exactly the failure mode task 2 warns about ("isSynthetic ever computed incorrectly, e.g. defaults to false when it should be true") - there is no default-to-false code path to accidentally take, because each concrete class hardcodes its own correct literal rather than inheriting or computing one.
task2_isSyntheticAdversarialAttack.additionalConfirmation: getStageCaller() was called directly (not mocked) in this credential-less sandbox and independently verified to return providerName='synthetic' and isSynthetic=true, then a full, completely unmodified default-routing verifyCompiledCandidate call (no reviewCaller override, no forceSemanticReview) on the same spurious-marker candidate was independently re-run and confirmed to stay at REVIEW_REQUIRED with the finding's severity still UNCERTAIN - ruling out the possibility that this behavior is a scripted-test-only artifact rather than what real, credential-less production traffic in this environment actually does today.
task2_isSyntheticAdversarialAttack.verdict: isSynthetic gating mechanism holds under direct adversarial attack. No defect found in this specific mechanism.
task2_isSyntheticAdversarialAttack.verifiedBy: tests/contract-model/part-b-recert-blocker9-independent-attack.test.ts - 'direct adversarial attack on isSynthetic gating' describe block (4 tests).

findings: downgradeUnconfirmedAmbiguousFindings's own function signature and body reference only `findings` (the already-merged deterministic+semantic finding array), `reconciliation` (Layer 1's own ReconciliationResult), and `review` (the Layer 2 reviewer's own SemanticReviewResult, specifically review.failed/isSynthetic/findings) - confirmed by direct string-search of the function body for compilationResult/overallNotes/sufficiencyReasons/unresolvedIssues, none of which appear.

dispositionRationale: Tasks 2 (isSynthetic gating), 3 (independence), and 4 (original 7-case reproduction) all hold under fresh, independent adversarial attack against the current, frozen production code - no defect found in any of those three mechanisms. However, task 1's own fresh construction of 12 novel condition-phrasing forms found that source-inventory.ts's CONDITIONAL_PHRASE detector - the single deterministic gate that determines whether a materially isolated, single-rule, numerically-clean candidate ever receives ANY independent scrutiny at all - still fails to detect 8 distinct, common, real-world credit-agreement condition idioms ('upon the occurrence of', 'as and when' + 'following', passive 'shall be deemed satisfied when', a bare defined-term-only trigger, a schedule-cross-reference-only incorporation, and non-numeric 'in the event of'/'in the event that'/'to the extent that'), and independently, concretely reproduced BLOCKER-9's exact original failure mode (a real qualifying condition silently dropped, reaching VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND with zero scrutiny from either verification layer) for all 8 forms under REAL, unmodified default production routing - not a hypothetical, a scripted override, or a Layer-1-only forced check. This is the same root-cause defect class BLOCKER-9 names, already found and partially patched twice in immediate succession (3F.1.6.R, then 3F.1.6.RX Part A itself), recurring a third time with different, equally common vocabulary. Per this Part B recertification's own explicit charter ('If you find a genuine defect, disposition STILL_OPEN or NEW_COUPLED_BLOCKER_DISCOVERED... If everything holds, disposition CERTIFIED_CLOSED'), a genuine, independently-reproduced defect squarely within BLOCKER-9's own charter was found, so CERTIFIED_CLOSED is not available; STILL_OPEN (not NEW_COUPLED_BLOCKER_DISCOVERED) is the correct disposition because this is not an architecturally distinct new defect - it is BLOCKER-9's own already-named failure mode, still open against a wider vocabulary than either prior remediation closed. Per the production-freeze rule in 22-recertification-baseline.json, no production code was modified to fix this - it is reported as evidence only, via the new, disclosed-as-defect-evidence test file above, for a human or a future remediation pass to act on.
